frs_sections.title: OVERVIEW
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================

Embedded DisplayPort (eDP) is the VESA digital display interface for the
INTERNAL panel connection inside a notebook, tablet, all-in-one (AIO), or
embedded system. eDP connects an on-board display Source (the GPU / SoC display
controller) to the INTEGRATED panel (the eDP Sink / Timing Controller, TCON)
over a short internal flex cable, replacing the legacy internal LVDS panel
interface.

eDP is built on the VESA DisplayPort base specification and reuses the same
three functional channels:

  * Main Link  — a uni-directional, high-bandwidth, isochronous channel that
                 carries the video stream from the Source to the panel Sink.
                 The Main Link is made of 1, 2, or 4 lanes, each a se…

frs_sections.title: Lane count
frs_sections.content:
The eDP Main Link is configurable to 1, 2, or 4 lanes. The negotiated lane count
is written to the LANE_COUNT_SET field of the DPCD. An embedded panel typically
uses 1, 2, or 4 lanes (ML_Lane0..ML_Lane3), each a differential pair
(ML_Lane0+/ML_Lane0- ... ML_Lane3+/ML_Lane3-) routed on the internal flex.

2.2 Link rates (link symbol rates per lane)
The Main Link operates at one of the standardized DisplayPort link rates. The
selected rate is written to the LINK_BW_SET field of the DPCD (or LINK_RATE_SET
for the higher rates):

  RBR  (Reduced Bit Rate) ........ 1.62 Gbps/lane   (8b/10b)
  HBR  (High Bit Rate) ........... 2.70 Gbps/lane   (8b/10b)
  HBR2 (High Bit Rate 2) ......... 5.40 Gbps/lane   (8b/10b)
  HBR3 (High Bit Rate 3) ......... 8.10 Gbps/lane   (8b/10b)

eDP also defines a set …

frs_sections.title: Channel coding
frs_sections.content:
For RBR/HBR/HBR2/HBR3 the Main Link uses ANSI 8b/10b coding: each 8-bit
character is encoded into a 10-bit DC-balanced, transition-rich symbol so the
panel Sink can recover the embedded link clock. The effective data efficiency of
8b/10b is 80%. The data is scrambled with an LFSR; on an eDP link the scrambler
is reset using the ASSR (Alternate Scrambler Seed Reset) seed instead of the
standard DisplayPort seed when ASSR is enabled (eDP_CONFIGURATION_CAP).

frs_sections.title: Symbols and control characters
frs_sections.content:
8b/10b control (K) symbols frame the stream: BS (Blanking Start), BE (Blanking
End), SR (Scrambler Reset), SS/SE (Secondary-data Start/End), FS/FE (Fill
Start/End), and the training pattern symbols. The blanking period between active
video lines carries the Main Stream Attributes (MSA) and secondary-data packets.

================================================================================
3. LINK TRAINING — FULL AND FAST LINK TRAINING
================================================================================

Before video can be transmitted the Source must train the Main Link so that the
panel Sink reliably recovers the data on every active lane. Link training is
performed over the AUX channel by writing the TRAINING_PATTERN_SET DPCD register
and reading back the LANE0_1_STATUS …

frs_sections.title: Electrical and coding
frs_sections.content:
The AUX channel is a single bidirectional, half-duplex differential pair
(AUX+/AUX-). It is AC-coupled and uses Manchester-II bi-phase encoding at a
nominal 1 Mbps. A request/reply transaction model is used: the Source (AUX
master) issues a request; the panel Sink (AUX slave) returns a reply. Each
transaction begins with a SYNC pattern (a preamble of consecutive zeros) and a
START/STOP condition delimiting the Manchester-coded payload.

frs_sections.title: Native AUX transactions
frs_sections.content:
Native AUX transactions read or write the panel's DPCD address space. The request
carries:
  * a 4-bit command (AUX command): native Read (1001b) / native Write (1000b),
    and I2C-over-AUX Read/Write/MOT variants;
  * a 20-bit address into the DPCD / I2C address space;
  * a length field (number of bytes minus one, 0..15 -> 1..16 bytes per
    transaction).
The reply carries a 4-bit AUX reply command: ACK / NACK / DEFER (and the
I2C-over-AUX equivalents I2C_ACK / I2C_NACK / I2C_DEFER).

4.3 DPCD — DisplayPort Configuration Data (with eDP-specific block)
DPCD is the panel Sink's configuration/status register space, accessed by native
AUX read/write. Key DPCD regions reused from DisplayPort:
  * Receiver Capability field (base address 00000h): DPCD_REV, MAX_LINK_RATE,
    MAX_LANE_COUNT, M…

frs_sections.title: I2C-over-AUX and EDID
frs_sections.content:
The panel's EDID (Extended Display Identification Data) is reached by tunneling
I2C transactions over AUX. The Source issues I2C-over-AUX read/write transactions
(with the MOT — Middle-Of-Transaction — bit to chain a multi-byte I2C burst)
addressed to the EDID I2C slave address (A0h/A1h). The 128-byte (or extended)
EDID block describes the panel's supported timings and capabilities.

================================================================================
5. PANEL SELF REFRESH (PSR / PSR2) AND THE REMOTE FRAME BUFFER (eDP-EXCLUSIVE)
================================================================================

5.1 The Remote Frame Buffer (RFB)
The DEFINING eDP power-saving feature is Panel Self Refresh (PSR). The panel
(eDP Sink / TCON) contains a local Remote Frame Buffer (RFB)…

frs_sections.title: PSR entry and exit
frs_sections.content:
* PSR ENTRY: the Source writes PSR_ENABLE / PSR_CONFIGURATION in the eDP DPCD,
    transmits a final frame, asserts a PSR-entry indication, and then quiesces
    the Main Link. The panel latches the last frame into the RFB and begins
    self-refreshing from the RFB.
  * PSR ACTIVE: the Main Link is idle / electrically quiescent; the panel
    refreshes from its RFB; the Source GPU may sleep.
  * PSR EXIT: on a screen update (or an IRQ_HPD), the Source re-establishes the
    Main Link (using Fast Link Training where possible), re-transmits the updated
    frame, and the panel returns to live (externally-driven) refresh.
The panel reports its PSR state in the eDP PSR_STATUS DPCD register.

frs_sections.title: PSR2 and selective update
frs_sections.content:
PSR2 extends PSR with SELECTIVE UPDATE: instead of re-transmitting the entire
frame on exit, the Source transmits only the changed rectangular region(s)
(Selective Update, SU region) into the RFB, further reducing Main Link activity
for small on-screen changes such as a blinking cursor or a clock. PSR2 also adds
frame-locking and early-transport options. PSR2 capability and configuration live
in the eDP DPCD (PSR2_ENABLE / PSR2 capability fields).

================================================================================
6. BACKLIGHT CONTROL OVER AUX (eDP-EXCLUSIVE)

frs_sections.title: MAIN STREAM ATTRIBUTES, TRANSFER UNITS, AND THE MICRO-PACKET STREAM
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================

8.1 Main Stream Attributes (MSA)
The MSA is a packet, transmitted once per video frame in the vertical blanking
interval, that describes the video stream: Mvid and Nvid (the time-stamp pair
used by asynchronous clocking to regenerate the pixel clock from the link clock),
Htotal/Vtotal, HSP/HSW, active width/height, MISC0/MISC1 (color format, bit
depth, dynamic range, colorimetry). eDP also supports a video-stream-clock mode
where the panel can run its own timing during PSR.

8.2 Transfer Units (TU)
The active video data of each scan line is packed into Transfer Units. A TU is a
fixed number of link symbols (typically 32 or 64 symbols per lane); within each
TU only as many symbols as required by the ratio of p…

frs_sections.title: Micro-packet framing
frs_sections.content:
Active line data is delimited by BS (Blanking Start) and BE (Blanking End)
control symbols. Secondary-data packets (audio sample packets, MSA, VSC SDP /
extended InfoFrames, PSR setup packets) are carried in the blanking intervals
delimited by SS/SE.

================================================================================

frs_sections.title: PINS / INTERNAL FLEX CONNECTION
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================

An eDP internal panel connection (flex cable / board-to-board connector)
exposes:
  * ML_Lane0(+/-), ML_Lane1(+/-), ML_Lane2(+/-), ML_Lane3(+/-) — up to four Main
    Link differential pairs (AC-coupled, self-clocked, embedded clock; 1/2/4
    used per panel).
  * AUX_CH(+/-) — one bidirectional half-duplex differential pair (Manchester-II,
    1 Mbps) for DPCD / link-training / I2C-over-AUX / backlight / PSR control.
  * HPD — Hot Plug Detect, a single-ended sideband input to the Source.
  * BL_PWM / BL_EN — optional backlight PWM and enable (when the backlight is not
    fully AUX-controlled).
  * VDD (panel logic), VBL (backlight), GND — panel and backlight power and
    ground.
There is NO external Displa…

frs_sections.title: STATE / LINK-POLICY SUMMARY
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================

The Source link-policy maker drives the embedded panel through:
  RESET/POWER_ON   -> HPD asserted by panel Sink
  CAPABILITY_READ  -> read DPCD Receiver Capability + eDP_CONFIGURATION_CAP
                      (ASSR / Fast Link Training / PSR caps)
  PANEL_POWER_ON   -> sequence panel VDD / backlight per panel power timing
  LINK_TRAINING    -> Fast Link Training (preferred) or full CR/EQ training
  ACTIVE           -> stream video as micro-packets / Transfer Units; MSA per
                      frame; set backlight brightness over AUX
  PSR_ACTIVE       -> on static screen, enter Panel Self Refresh: panel refreshes
                      from the RFB while the Main Link sleeps
  PSR_EXIT         -> on update…

frs_sections.title: REVISION HISTORY
frs_sections.content:
================================================================================

  eDP 1.0  (2008) — first embedded variant of DisplayPort for internal panels.
  eDP 1.1  (2009) — backlight control, ASSR, additional panel power features.
  eDP 1.2  (2010) — additional link rates, multi-touch sideband.
  eDP 1.3  (2011) — Panel Self Refresh (PSR) introduced; Remote Frame Buffer.
  eDP 1.4  (2013) — PSR2 (selective update), additional link rates, Display
                    Stream Compression (DSC), reduced-swing electrical option.
  eDP 1.4a (2015) — PSR2 selective-update clarifications.
  eDP 1.4b (2015) — corrections / errata.
  eDP 1.5  (2021) — Panel Replay alignment with DP 2.0, enhanced PSR2, additional
                    panel power-optimization features.

protocol_overview.type: VESA embedded digital display interface (Embedded DisplayPort). Source -> single internal-panel Sink isochronous video over a packetized Main Link (1/2/4 self-clocked differential lanes), with a bidirectional half-duplex AUX channel for management (DPCD / link training / I2C-over-AUX EDID / backlight-over-AUX / PSR control) and a Hot Plug Detect (HPD) sideband.
protocol_overview.duplex: Main Link is uni-directional (Source -> panel). AUX channel is bidirectional half-duplex (request from Source, reply from panel Sink over the same pair). HPD is a Sink -> Source sideband.
protocol_overview.encoding: Main Link: ANSI 8b/10b for RBR/HBR/HBR2/HBR3 (DC-balanced, transition-rich, 80% efficient, LFSR-scrambled with the ASSR alternate seed when enabled) with the clock embedded and recovered by the panel Sink during training. AUX channel: Manchester-II bi-phase at ~1 Mbps.
protocol_overview.modulation: NRZ (two-level) differential on Main Link and AUX.

aux_channel.model: request/reply native AUX transactions into DPCD; I2C-over-AUX for EDID; backlight-over-AUX; PSR control

link_training.full_phase_1: Clock Recovery (CR) — TPS1, adjust voltage swing / pre-emphasis until CR_DONE on all active lanes
link_training.full_phase_2: Channel Equalization (EQ) — TPS2/3/4, until CHANNEL_EQ_DONE + SYMBOL_LOCKED + INTERLANE_ALIGN_DONE
link_training.fast_link_training: FLT — apply stored drive/rate/lane settings and send training patterns for a short fixed interval (fixed embedded channel)
link_training.control: over AUX via TRAINING_PATTERN_SET and per-lane status readback in DPCD
link_training.fallback: FLT -> full CR/EQ; then lower link rate and/or fewer lanes

protocol_overview.stream_framing: micro-packet stream: Main Stream Attributes (MSA) per frame, Transfer Units (TU) for active video, BS/BE blanking-symbol framing, secondary-data (audio / SDP / PSR-setup) packets in the blanking intervals.

edp_exclusive_features.panel_self_refresh: PSR / PSR2 — panel refreshes from a local Remote Frame Buffer (RFB) while the Source and Main Link sleep; PSR2 adds selective update.
edp_exclusive_features.remote_frame_buffer: RFB — panel-local store of the last frame.
edp_exclusive_features.backlight_over_aux: Panel backlight brightness set via eDP backlight DPCD registers (PWM + AUX brightness).
edp_exclusive_features.assr: Alternate Scrambler Seed Reset — eDP scrambler seed for content protection.
edp_exclusive_features.fast_link_training: Abbreviated training for the fixed embedded channel.

compliance_requirements: Main Link of 1/2/4 self-clocked AC-coupled differential lanes with 8b/10b coding (RBR..HBR3) and embedded clock.
Bidirectional half-duplex Manchester-II AUX channel with the native AUX request/reply transaction model.
DPCD register space (Receiver Capability / Link Configuration / Link Status) plus the eDP-specific DPCD block (eDP_CONFIGURATION_CAP / backlight / PSR).
Link Training: full two-phase CR/EQ and Fast Link Training (FLT).
Panel Self Refresh (PSR / PSR2) with a Remote Frame Buffer (RFB).
Backlight control over AUX (eDP backlight DPCD registers / PWM).
ASSR (Alternate Scrambler Seed Reset) when enabled.
Single embedded panel Sink — NO Multi-Stream Transport, NO external connector.
Hot Plug Detect (HPD) including IRQ_HPD short-pulse event signaling.

functional_requirements.text: An eDP link comprises three channels: a uni-directional Main Link (1/2/4 lanes) for video, a bidirectional half-duplex AUX channel for management, and a Hot Plug Detect (HPD) sideband — connecting the Source to a single internal panel Sink.
The Main Link is configurable to 1, 2, or 4 lanes (LANE_COUNT_SET in DPCD); each lane is a self-clocked AC-coupled differential pair on the internal flex.
The Main Link runs at one of RBR 1.62, HBR 2.7, HBR2 5.4, or HBR3 8.1 Gbps/lane (8b/10b), set in LINK_BW_SET (eDP may also use intermediate eDP link rates from the eDP supported-rates table).
RBR/HBR/HBR2/HBR3 use ANSI 8b/10b coding (DC-balanced, transition-rich, LFSR-scrambled) with the clock embedded; the ASSR alternate scrambler seed is used when enabled.

Before video the Source trains the Main Link, either by Fast Link Training (apply stored drive settings for the fixed channel) or by full two-phase Clock Recovery + Channel Equalization, falling back FLT -> full -> lower rate/lane on failure.
The AUX channel is a bidirectional half-duplex differential pair using Manchester-II coding at ~1 Mbps with a request/reply transaction model (4-bit command, 20-bit address, length).
Native AUX transactions read/write the panel's DPCD (Receiver Capability 00000h, Link Configuration 00100h, Link/Sink Status 00200h) AND the eDP-specific DPCD block at 00700h.
I2C-over-AUX tunnels I2C transactions (MOT bit chains bursts) to read the panel EDID (I2C address A0h).

eDP provides Panel Self Refresh (PSR): the panel stores the last frame in a local Remote Frame Buffer (RFB) and refreshes from it while the Source and Main Link sleep; PSR2 adds selective update of only the changed region. PSR is controlled via the eDP DPCD (PSR_ENABLE / PSR_CONFIGURATION / PSR_STATUS).

eDP controls the panel backlight over AUX via the eDP backlight DPCD registers (EDP_BACKLIGHT_MODE_SET, EDP_BACKLIGHT_BRIGHTNESS, EDP_PWMGEN_BIT_COUNT, EDP_BACKLIGHT_FREQ_SET) and/or a backlight PWM pin.

eDP supports ASSR (Alternate Scrambler Seed Reset): when enabled (eDP_CONFIGURATION_CAP) the Main Link scrambler is reset with the alternate seed for content protection between the co-designed Source and panel.

eDP does NOT implement Multi-Stream Transport: the embedded panel is a single Sink, so there are no virtual channels, no MST time-slot table, and no branch / daisy-chain devices; there is no external connector.
The panel Sink drives HPD to indicate presence; a short HPD pulse (IRQ_HPD) signals link-status-change or PSR-state-change events requiring a status re-read.

error_response_conditions: AUX reply NACK / DEFER — panel rejects or defers a native AUX transaction; the Source retries.
I2C-over-AUX I2C_NACK / I2C_DEFER — the tunneled EDID I2C ROM NACKs/defers.
Fast Link Training failure — stored settings do not lock; fall back to full CR/EQ training.
Clock Recovery failure — a lane never reports CR_DONE; raise swing/pre-emphasis or fall back rate/lane-count.
Channel Equalization failure — CHANNEL_EQ_DONE / SYMBOL_LOCKED / INTERLANE_ALIGN_DONE not all set; fall back and re-train.
PSR exit failure — panel fails to re-establish the link on update; the Source re-trains (Fast Link Training) and re-transmits.
